---
title: Nebius Serverless Jobs
description: Fine-tune a model on Nebius GPUs with Axolotl, save the outputs and resume training
---

[Nebius Serverless Jobs](https://docs.nebius.com/serverless/jobs/manage) runs
Axolotl training on a fresh GPU VM. Choose your GPU in a cloud YAML, pass your
training config to `axolotl train --cloud`, and the Nebius CLI launches the job
and streams its logs. Checkpoints and final weights are exported to object storage.

This experimental integration supports single-node training. The example below
runs a 30-step LoRA fine-tune on one H100 with a public model and dataset.
For multi-node training or SkyPilot-managed clusters, see the [SkyPilot guide](skypilot.qmd).

## Setup {#prerequisites}

Install [Axolotl](installation.qmd) with the Nebius provider and the
[Nebius CLI](https://docs.nebius.com/cli/install) on the machine you submit from.
Authenticate and check that your CLI includes `ai job run` (tested with 0.12.265):

```bash
nebius auth login
nebius ai job run --help
```

Your Nebius project needs GPU quota, available capacity and a subnet for the
selected GPU. See the [Jobs prerequisites](https://docs.nebius.com/serverless/jobs/manage).
Training runs in the remote container; local Nebius credentials are not uploaded.

## Launch training

Create `nebius.yaml` to describe where the job runs. Replace `project-YOUR_PROJECT_ID`
with your project ID and choose a platform/preset available there:

```yaml
provider: nebius
parent_id: project-YOUR_PROJECT_ID
image: axolotlai/axolotl@sha256:a667b20750d07944468192d0c1b7c75222df6cc179cfc77061abc959aff7e9ab
platform: gpu-h100-sxm
preset: 1gpu-16vcpu-200gb
timeout: 3600
output: auto
```

This image was validated on H100; see [tested configuration](#tested-configuration)
for its runtime versions. Add `subnet_id` if you need a specific subnet, or `profile`
to use a different CLI profile. The timeout is in seconds and includes provisioning
and image startup. `output: auto` selects the CLI's managed project bucket.

Download the [example training config](https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl/blob/main/examples/nebius-serverless/lora-1b.yml)
as `train.yml`, then launch it:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl/main/examples/nebius-serverless/lora-1b.yml -o train.yml
axolotl train train.yml --cloud nebius.yaml
```

The training config selects the model, dataset and LoRA settings; `nebius.yaml`
selects the cloud resources. You can replace `train.yml` with your own Axolotl
config. Training overrides and `--launcher` options are forwarded to the remote run.

The CLI prints the job ID, job name and output location, then follows training
until it ends. Keep these values to inspect the job or retrieve its outputs.
**Ctrl+C stops following logs; it does not cancel the remote job.**

Only the training config, launcher settings and bootstrap files are uploaded.
Local datasets, Python modules and config includes are not copied. Use Hub data or
[mounted storage](#dataset-inputs-and-secrets), and include dependencies in the image.

## Logs and cancellation {#status-cancellation-and-cleanup}

Replace `JOB_ID` with the ID printed at launch. Use the same CLI profile as submission:

```bash
nebius ai job get JOB_ID --format json
nebius ai job logs JOB_ID --follow
```

To stop training:

```bash
nebius ai job cancel JOB_ID
```

Nebius manages VM and boot-disk cleanup. Output buckets and mounted data remain
until you remove them. Confirm compute cleanup through the Nebius Console or API;
a terminal job state alone does not prove deletion has finished. See the
[Nebius job lifecycle](https://docs.nebius.com/serverless/lifecycle).

## Download outputs {#outputs-and-checkpoints}

The example sets `output_dir: training`. Each submission has its own output prefix,
usually `runs/JOB_NAME/training/` in the selected bucket. Use the location printed
by the CLI to find the actual bucket and prefix.

After [configuring S3 credentials and the AWS CLI](https://docs.nebius.com/object-storage/interfaces/aws-cli),
download the outputs:

```bash
aws --endpoint-url https://storage.REGION.nebius.cloud \
  s3 cp s3://BUCKET/runs/JOB_NAME/training/ ./downloaded-training/ --recursive
```

Replace `REGION`, `BUCKET` and `JOB_NAME` with your output location. S3 credentials
are separate from your Nebius CLI login. For LoRA, load the downloaded adapter
with the same base model and tokenizer revisions used for training.

Completed checkpoint exports include `nebius-checkpoint.json`; a normally completed
run exports its final weights and `nebius-result.json`. These manifests list file
sizes and SHA-256 hashes. A checkpoint directory without a complete, valid manifest
cannot be used for resume.

Checkpoints are saved on the VM's local disk before being copied to the bucket.
`save_total_limit` controls local retention only; exported checkpoints remain until
you delete them. Size `disk_size` for model caches, local checkpoints and any restored
checkpoint. Export failures stop training rather than continue without that checkpoint.

## Resume training {#resume-explicitly}

To resume a checkpoint in a new Job, add the previous output bucket to `nebius.yaml`
at a separate read-only mount:

```yaml
volumes:
  - source: storagebucket-YOUR_OUTPUT_BUCKET
    mount: /previous
    mode: ro
```

Update `train.yml` with the chosen checkpoint path:

```yaml
resume_from_checkpoint: /previous/runs/PREVIOUS_JOB_NAME/training/checkpoint-10
auto_resume_from_checkpoints: false
save_only_model: false
```

Keep the same model/tokenizer revisions, dataset order, adapter settings and training
schedule, then submit again:

```bash
axolotl train train.yml --cloud nebius.yaml
```

The new Job writes to its own output prefix. Before training, it copies the checkpoint
to local disk, verifies the manifest's sizes/hashes and checks for weights, Trainer,
optimizer, scheduler and RNG state. These checks do not establish compatibility
with a different model or training config.

Automatic checkpoint selection and recovery after preemption are not supported.
Choose an earlier complete checkpoint if verification fails. Adapter weights alone
are insufficient to restore training state; distributed/sharded checkpoints are
outside the current resume support.

## Datasets and secrets {#dataset-inputs-and-secrets}

Public Hub datasets work with the ordinary Axolotl dataset loader. For files in a
Nebius bucket, add a mount to `nebius.yaml`:

```yaml
volumes:
  - source: storagebucket-YOUR_INPUT_BUCKET
    mount: /data
    mode: ro
```

Reference the mounted path in `train.yml`:

```yaml
datasets:
  - path: /data/train.jsonl
    ds_type: json
    type: alpaca
```

Mounts must use absolute container paths and cannot overlap each other or `/outputs`.
The provider uses existing volumes; it does not create custom volumes or their IAM credentials.

For gated models or private Hub datasets, create a Nebius secret with a payload
entry named `HF_TOKEN`, then reference its ID in `nebius.yaml`:

```yaml
env_secret:
  HF_TOKEN: mbsec-YOUR_SECRET_ID
```

Use the secret ID, not the token value. With CLI 0.12.265, the environment variable
name selects the payload key; the advertised `secret-id/key` form was rejected in
validation. Local environment variables are not automatically passed to the job.
Nonsecret variables can be set through `env`, for example:

```yaml
env:
  HF_HOME: /tmp/huggingface
```

See the [dataset loading guide](dataset_loading.qmd) for other formats. Direct S3
dataset access requires its own credentials and endpoint configuration.

## Custom images {#runtime-images-and-local-forks}

Use a [plain Axolotl image](docker.qmd) compatible with your GPU driver and pin its
digest for repeatable runs. To include a local fork or plugins, replace `image` in
`nebius.yaml` with a build configuration:

```yaml
image_build:
  context: ../my-axolotl-fork
  dockerfile: Dockerfile
  tag: registry.example.com/team/axolotl:my-fork
  platform: linux/amd64
```

The context is relative to the cloud YAML. Docker builds and pushes the tagged image
before submission; the Dockerfile must install your fork and plugins. Configure
registry access so Nebius can pull the image: your local Docker push credentials
are not uploaded as remote pull credentials. Builds require a tag and `linux/amd64`.
See [shared image configuration](custom_integrations.qmd#selecting-or-building-the-runtime-image).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What to do |
|---|---|
| `NotEnoughResources` | The requested GPU could not be provisioned. Check capacity for your platform/preset and retry after confirming the previous Job is terminal. |
| `TimeoutExceeded` | Increase `timeout` in the cloud YAML; allow for provisioning and image startup as well as training. |
| Local data or modules are missing | Mount the data or include dependencies in the image; the working directory is not uploaded. |
| Checkpoint verification fails | Select an earlier complete checkpoint with its manifest and full training state. |
| CLI exits or log following is interrupted | Query the job state before resubmitting. The remote job may still be running. |

For a local packaging preview, add `show_context: true` to `nebius.yaml` and run the
same launch command. Remove it to submit training. `dry_run: true` instead requests
server-side validation; the two options are mutually exclusive and require a prebuilt
`image`. On CLI 0.12.265, managed-output dry runs failed with
`unsupported volume source type "nebius"`; use `show_context` on that release.
The CLI limits the compressed upload context to 64 KiB.

On a CLI failure, Axolotl attempts one read-only status lookup and reports guidance
for the returned state. It never automatically resubmits or cancels the job.
If you lost the job ID, use `nebius ai job list` or `nebius ai job get-by-name --help`
to locate the job by its printed name.

## Configuration reference

| Cloud key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `provider` | `nebius` |
| `image` / `image_build` | Prebuilt runtime or tagged local Docker build (choose one) |
| `platform`, `preset` | Required explicit GPU resource choice |
| `profile`, `parent_id`, `subnet_id` | Optional CLI profile/project/subnet selection |
| `disk_size` | Optional VM disk size, such as `250Gi` |
| `timeout` | Seconds; defaults to 86400, allowed range 3600–604800 |
| `output` | Output bucket ID/name, supported S3 URI, or `auto` (default) |
| `volumes` | List of `source`, `mount`, and optional `mode` (`ro` or `rw`) |
| `env` | Mapping of nonsecret environment variables to string values |
| `env_secret` | Mapping of environment variables to Nebius secret references |
| `show_context` | Local packaging preview; no submission |
| `dry_run` | Server-side request validation; no Job creation |

Unknown cloud keys are rejected. Dataset preprocessing runs inside the training
Job; separate remote preprocessing and lm-eval are not supported.

## Tested configuration

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Runtime and validation scope — September 11, 2026

The pinned image above was tested on H100 in `eu-north1` with
`gpu-h100-sxm` / `1gpu-16vcpu-200gb` and Nebius CLI 0.12.265. It reported Python
3.12.13, Torch 2.12.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Transformers 5.16.1 and PEFT 0.20.0;
the host driver was 580.173.02. The base model was `NousResearch/Llama-3.2-1B`,
with this revision pinned for validation:

```yaml
revision_of_model: a9745ffc3556f145a830ac0c203509ba860582a3
```

The 30-step LoRA run, independent export size/hash checks, adapter loading and
fresh-Job resume with optimizer/scheduler/RNG restoration passed. A separate CPU
probe verified a one-hour timeout including provisioning and image startup.

These observations cover one configuration. File close and a manifest written
last do not establish a remote-flush barrier or an atomic directory transaction.
Resume checks file integrity; bit-identical training across runs is not guaranteed.
:::
